script: Your dog howls when you leave, destroys the door, or has accidents even though they are house trained. That can be separation anxiety, which is real distress, not spite. Common signs include barking or howling soon after you leave, drooling, pacing, chewing near exits, and following you from room to room. A dog who is only bored usually settles after a while, while an anxious dog stays distressed. What helps? First, teach calm alone time in tiny steps. Leave for a few seconds, come back before your dog panics, and slowly build up. Second, keep departures and arrivals low key, because big emotional goodbyes can raise excitement. Third, give your dog exercise and a food puzzle before you go, which helps them relax. Fourth, never punish a dog for what happens while you are away, because that adds fear to the problem. Short, predictable routines build confidence, and progress is usually slow but steady. If your dog is extremely distressed, hurts themselves, or does not improve, talk to your veterinarian or a certified behavior professional, since some dogs need extra support.
